title: AI Agent Bootcamp
description: Build agents that turn repetitive work into reliable, useful workflows. From your first prompt to a project you can share.
audience: Curious professionals and aspiring AI builders. No AI experience needed.
outcome: An evaluated AI agent and a portfolio-ready capstone.

lessons.title: From prompts to useful systems
lessons.content: A prompt gives a model instructions. A workflow connects explicit steps. An agent selects tools to pursue a goal. Start with a workflow when the steps are predictable. Add agency only when a decision requires it.
lessons.task: Write down a repetitive task, its input, its desired output, and one condition that requires human review.

lessons.title: Your first structured prompt
lessons.content: A useful prompt includes a role, task, relevant context, constraints, and an output format. Test it against both normal and ambiguous examples. Treat model output as untrusted until checked.
lessons.task: Draft a prompt that extracts action items from meeting notes. Test it with missing dates and unclear owners.

lessons.title: Give your agent a tool
lessons.content: Tools expose narrow functions with validated inputs. Keep credentials on the server. Read-only tools are a good starting point; actions that change external data need an explicit approval step.
lessons.task: Design a read-only search tool: define its input schema, expected output, and failure behavior.

lessons.title: Ground answers with retrieval
lessons.content: Retrieval finds relevant source passages before generation. Split documents by meaningful sections, retain source references, and test whether the retrieved passages actually answer the question.
lessons.task: Create five questions about a document. Record the passage that supports each answer and one unanswerable question.

lessons.title: Test the unhappy path
lessons.content: A demo is not an evaluation. Make a small dataset of expected behaviors. Include irrelevant context, missing inputs, malicious instructions in documents, and provider outages.
lessons.task: Create a ten-case evaluation checklist. Define pass/fail criteria before running it.

lessons.title: Deploy your capstone
lessons.content: Package the API, frontend, and database with Docker. Keep secrets out of source control. Add health checks, logs, rate limits, backups, and human review for consequential actions.
lessons.task: Publish a repository README with setup instructions, examples, limitations, and your evaluation results.

title: AI Workshops
description: Make room for a small idea. Leave with a working prototype, a repeatable workflow, and a clear next step.
audience: Anyone ready to move from experimenting to making.
outcome: A practical app blueprint and a tested prototype.

lessons.title: Choose a problem worth solving
lessons.content: Choose one user and one task. Interview that user, observe their current workflow, and write a testable statement of success. A narrow useful prototype teaches more than a broad unfinished product.
lessons.task: Write a problem statement in the form: For [user], help [task], measured by [outcome].

lessons.title: Build with the GenAI Accelerator
lessons.content: Use the Accelerator to turn your problem brief into a project checklist. The starter Accelerator is a guided template, not an AI generator. Use its deliverables to plan your first prototype.
lessons.task: Open the Accelerator, save a project brief, and choose the smallest end-to-end feature.

lessons.title: Get comfortable in the terminal
lessons.content: A terminal lets you navigate files and run tools. pwd shows your location, ls lists files, and cat reads a file. The Terminal Tutor here simulates a safe set of commands.
lessons.task: Open Terminal Tutor. Run pwd, ls, and cat README.md. Explain what each command does.

lessons.title: Demo, reflect, improve
lessons.content: A strong demo shows the problem, one representative input, the resulting output, and what still fails. Ask a peer to try your prototype without instructions.
lessons.task: Record a two-minute demo and write down three improvements based on feedback.

title: Freelancing Masterclass
description: Turn practical AI skills into a focused service. Find your niche, scope your offer, and build a credible portfolio.
audience: Professionals exploring independent work with AI.
outcome: A service offer, discovery brief, and portfolio case study.

lessons.title: Find your service niche
lessons.content: Start with an industry you understand and a recurring workflow with a measurable cost. Avoid promising accuracy or savings before you have evidence.
lessons.task: List three industries you know and one recurring problem in each. Pick one to research.

lessons.title: Run a discovery conversation
lessons.content: Ask about the current process, frequency, data sensitivity, decision makers, and what a successful result looks like. Define what is outside scope and who approves changes.
lessons.task: Write five discovery questions and a one-page statement of work with acceptance criteria.

lessons.title: Build a portfolio case study
lessons.content: Show the original problem, your approach, measurable results, and limitations. Get permission before using any client information. A self-directed project is a valid first case study.
lessons.task: Write a case study using a synthetic example. Include your evaluation method and a clear limitation.
